## How they got there
Inter finished as runners-up in the 2024-25 Champions League after losing the final to Paris Saint-Germain 0-5. During the league phase, their profile was defined by exceptional efficiency, with a Points per game value of 2.38 that placed them better than 94% of teams. They also secured their position through defensive solidity, recording an Opponent shots on target per game of 2.9 which beat 89% of their peers, alongside a Goal difference per game of 1.25 that surpassed 88% of teams.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would not have selected Inter for the final, as they ranked ninth among knockout teams and fell outside its top two choices. With a probability of 7.7%, their chances were slightly below the base rate of 8.3% for a random team to reach the final. The stage on that scale nearest to the model's expectation was quarter-finals. While Long passes (% of passes) at 11.1 contributed positively with a SHAP value of 0.14, the prediction was pulled down by Attacks per game (value 38.4, contribution -0.16).

## Weak spots
Shot accuracy (% on target) had a value of 39.2 and beat only 8% of that season's teams. Attacks per game recorded a value of 38.4 and beat 35% of that season's teams. Shot conversion (% of shots scored) stood at 13.9 and beat 36% of that season's teams.

A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Use 'significant' or 'significantly' only for a Holm-adjusted p-value comparison, never for other differences. Write plain markdown without tables.
